subject: Warnings (?) from a varying-intercept, varying-slope linear model with a categorical predictor

messages.author: b8264485dc7f85ef
messages.subject: Warnings (?) from a varying-intercept, varying-slope linear model with a categorical predictor
parts:
Dear all, 

I recently started trying out Stan via Rstan. I built a model like below based on this guide.

data {
 int<lower=0> N;                     //total # of observations
 int<lower=0> NS;                    //total # of subjects
 int<lower=0> NI;                    //total # of experimental items
 int<lower=1, upper=NS> subject[N];  //Subject ID
 int<lower=1, upper=NI> item[N];     //Item ID
 vector[N] cond;                     //Categorical predictor (3 levels)
 vector[N] rt;                       //Outcome variable (reaction time)
 vector[2] zero;                     //A vector of 0's
}


parameters {
 vector[2] beta;              //intercept and slope
 vector[2] u[NS];             //subject random effects
 vector[2] w[NI];             //item random effects
 real<lower=0> sigma_e;       //residual sd
 vector<lower=0>[2] sigma_u;  //subject sd
 vector<lower=0>[2] sigma_w;  //item sd
 corr_matrix[2] omega_u;      //correlation matrix for subject random effects
 corr_matrix[2] omega_w;      //correlation matrix for item random effects
}

transformed parameters{
 cov_matrix[2] Sigma_u;       //VCV matrix for subject random effects
 cov_matrix[2] Sigma_w;       //VCV matrix for item random effects
 for(r in 1:2){
   for(c in 1:2){
     Sigma_u[r, c] <- sigma_u[r] * sigma_u[c] * omega_u[r, c];
     Sigma_w[r, c] <- sigma_w[r] * sigma_w[c] * omega_w[r, c];
   }
 }
}


model{
 real mu[N];
 for(j in 1:NS){
   u[j] ~ multi_normal(zero, Sigma_u);
 }
 for(k in 1:NI){
   w[k] ~ multi_normal(zero, Sigma_w);
 }
 
 sigma_u ~ gamma(1.5, 1.0E-4);
 sigma_w ~ gamma(1.5, 1.0E-4);
 sigma_e ~ gamma(1.5, 1.0E-4);

 omega_u ~lkj_corr(2.0);
 omega_w ~lkj_corr(2.0);


 for(i in 1:N){
   mu[i] <- (beta[1] + u[subject[i], 1] + w[item[i], 1]) +
            (beta[2] + u[subject[i], 2] + w[item[i], 2])*cond[i];
 }

 rt ~ normal(mu, sigma_e);
}



When I ran the model, I got messages shown below. I wonder what may have caused it. Also, I have a 3-level categorical predictor. I wonder if it needs to be manually dummy coded. The session info is at the end of the post, and files containing the Stan model code, the dataset, and the R code to run the Stan code are attached to this post. Thank you!

parts:
What makes you think there's a problem? It's OK to get a few
of those messages during warmup. You can try to crank down the
initial step size lower (say 0.001), which should avoid some of
these messages during warmup. The problem is that the discretization
of the Hamiltonian needs to find the right step size before
things become arithmetically stable.

What did the output look like? Can you get it to fit simulated
data?

- Bob

parts:
Thanks for the quick reply. The red font of the message made me a bit paranoid...that's why I thought there were problems. I printed the output, and based on the output, I think I made the mistake of coding the 3-level predictor as one variable (the 3 levels were coded as 1, 2, and 3). I thought Stan would automatically dummy code it as R would. This might explain why there were only two betas in my initial output, as shown below. I dummy coded the predictor, and re-ran the model. The new results (as shown by the output at the bottom of this reply) seem reasonable.

On Tuesday, December 23, 2014 1:40:29 PM UTC-8, Bob Carpenter wrote:
What makes you think there's a problem?  It's OK to get a few
of those messages during warmup.  You can try to crank down the
initial step size lower (say 0.001), which should avoid some of
these messages during warmup.  The problem is that the discretization
of the Hamiltonian needs to find the right step size before
things become arithmetically stable.

What did the output look like?  Can you get it to fit simulated
data?

- Bob
